_about: Single authoritative release record; every page reads release facts from here. `current` names the release the site features; older releases stay in `releases` as version history. A release is public only when `status` is "released" AND the owner has approved it: then `date`, `sha256` and its `method`'s fields must all be set (the build refuses anything else). `method`: `discord` = the official release post on the Project Blonde Discord (`download.url` is that post's permanent link, never a signed attachment URL); `patcher` = made in the visitor's browser from content/patcher.json. `public_version` must equal blonde/release/public-version.json and the title screen. v1.2 facts are copied from output/project-blonde-v1.2-rc2-20261011/release-information.json and its guides, v1.1 facts from output/project-blonde-v1.1-rc-v111-20261010/release-information.json. A previous release keeps its record here: `post_removed` (the day its download post was removed; never linked) or `discord_post` (its download post is still on the Discord, kept with the owner's approval when v1.3 was released). v1.3 facts are copied from output/project-blonde-v1.3-rc1-20261017/ (release-information.json, RELEASE-MANIFEST.json and its guides); v1.4 facts from output/project-blonde-v1.4-rc1-20261019/ (release-information.json, RELEASE-MANIFEST.json, VERIFICATION-SUMMARY.txt and its guides). When v1.4 was released the v1.3 post was kept on the Discord (discord_post); the v1.2 post had already been removed. No URL, date, checksum or patch detail is invented here. v1.4.2 facts are copied from output/project-blonde-v1.4.2-20261103/ (release-information.json, RELEASE-MANIFEST.json and its guides); when v1.4.2 was released the v1.4.1 and v1.4 posts were kept on the Discord (discord_post). v1.4.3 facts are copied from output/project-blonde-v1.4.3-20261106/ (release-information.json, RELEASE-MANIFEST.json and its guides); when v1.4.3 was released the v1.4.2, v1.4.1 and v1.4 posts were kept on the Discord (discord_post).

file.type: ZIP with one Game Boy Advance game (.gba)

releases.save_compatibility: No save-format change. Saves from v1.0, v1.1, v1.2, v1.3, v1.4, v1.4.1 and v1.4.2 were loaded with Continue in v1.4.3, opened the portable PC, saved again inside the game and reloaded with party, boxes and Frontier data unchanged. Tested in mGBA; not tested on Delta on a device, on an Android device or on physical hardware.
releases.save_compatibility_short: Saves from v1.0 to v1.4.2 continue with an ordinary Continue. Back up first.
highlights: Large followers such as HO-OH and LUGIA no longer glitch after your lead Pokémon faints.
DexNav no longer crashes when hunting WEEZING on Cinnabar Island.
Portable Pokémon PC: press R on the party screen to open Pokémon Storage wherever supported. HP, PP and status conditions stay as they are.
Overworld wild encounters: see wild Pokémon in the grass, caves and water of every region, and battle the one you walk into. Optional; CLASSIC stays the default.
Primal Reversion: Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon, with the Red and Blue Orbs from May and Brendan after the Silph Conspiracy.
One-time legendaries you have caught stay caught after League wins.
The Silph Conspiracy, partner battles and a new Elite Four member.
Johto, Kanto and Hoenn in one adventure, with Mega Evolution, the DexNav and Pokémon that follow you.
changelog: Followers: when your lead Pokémon faints in battle and a large Pokémon such as HO-OH or LUGIA becomes your follower, it no longer appears as a block of glitched graphics. It comes out of its Poké Ball and follows you normally.
Followers: a new follower after healing, reordering your party or changing maps also loads its graphics correctly.
Overworld encounters (optional): your follower now takes priority on a crowded screen. A few wild Pokémon may step away to make room and come back as you move on. Shiny wild Pokémon are kept.
Everything in v1.4.2 remains, including the DexNav fix and the portable Pokémon PC.
The title screen still shows v1.4. This is intentional.
known_limitations: The portable PC opens MOVE POKéMON. MOVE ITEMS stays on Pokémon Center PCs.
PC storage stays at 14 boxes (420 Pokémon). The save memory of a GBA cartridge is full; more boxes would need a save-format change and are planned for a future update.

Overworld encounters (optional): on very busy screens a single frame can occasionally be dropped, as in CLASSIC. An area you can only reach by Surf still counts as reachable, so Pokémon may appear there before you have Surf. DexNav can sometimes report that the Pokémon could not be found nearby; try again.

Legendaries: for a legendary without its own "caught" record, one that was caught and then released or traded away can no longer be recognised and may reappear after a League win. Copies created by League wins in older versions are kept.
A GS BALL you already collected again in an older version stays in your bag.

Overworld encounters (optional): while HO-OH, LUGIA or another large Pokémon follows you on a crowded screen, fewer wild Pokémon are visible at once (as when you arrive with it already following). If a Pokémon faints from poison while you walk (only when SURVIVE POISON is off in the challenge options), nearby wild Pokémon may step away with a puff of dust or grass.
v1.4.3 was tested in the mGBA 0.10.5 engine on a computer. It was not tested on Delta on a device, on an Android device or on original GBA hardware.
notes: Public version v1.4.3, internal build r11. The title screen still shows v1.4; this is intentional.
Released on 6 November 2026 on the Project Blonde Discord.

v1.4.3 is a bug-fix update: large followers such as HO-OH and LUGIA no longer glitch after your lead Pokémon faints, and a new follower always loads its graphics correctly. Everything in v1.4.2 remains, including the DexNav fix and the portable Pokémon PC.
This guide’s data was read from v1.4. v1.4.3 changes no maps, trainers, items or wild Pokémon, so it applies unchanged.

v1.4.3 was checked in focused release tests on the release build: followers after a faint, healing, party changes and save + reload, crowded overworld-encounter screens and shiny wild Pokémon, battles with visible wild Pokémon, busy towns, DexNav, the portable PC, and saves from every earlier version, in the mGBA engine.

instructions: Back up the old game and its normal in-game save.
Use your platform guide: matching mGBA / RetroArch file names, or Delta import/export.
Cold launch and choose CONTINUE; do not transfer an old save state.
Verify party, bag, badges, money and location, then save and back up again.
facts: Use Continue from a cold launch. Do not carry an emulator save state across this update. If you only have a save state, load it in the old version and make a normal in-game save first.
A save made inside a building or town shows that place as it was in the old version. Leave and re-enter, and it updates. Nothing is lost.

The game file is still named Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba. Keep the matching save name: Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav in mGBA, Pokemon - Project Blonde.srm in RetroArch. If your files use another name, keep that matching pair on copies; do not rename or overwrite your only backup.
If Continue is missing, stop and check the imported save or the save path before starting a new game.
The title screen still shows v1.4 after updating. This is intentional.
To go back, restore v1.4.2 with its own pre-update save backup.

guides.name: iPhone & iPad
steps: In the old game, use the game’s SAVE command. Return to Delta’s library.
Long-press the old game: Manage Save File → Export Save File. Save a dated backup in Files. Keep the old game and this backup.
Download the ZIP from the official Discord downloads post and extract it in Files. In Delta, tap + and import Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba. It may appear as a separate library entry.
Long-press the new game: Manage Save File → Import Save File. Select a copy of your exported save.
Cold-launch the new game, check the v1.4 label, then choose Continue. Check party, Bag, Badges, money and location.
Save inside the game and export a fresh backup. Keep the pre-update backup too.
guides.note: Use the normal save, not an emulator save state. If Continue is missing, check the save import before starting New Game. Delta accepts a save of exactly 131,072 bytes; a save exported from Delta already is, and a save from mGBA on a computer (131,088 bytes) must be trimmed first. This procedure was written from Delta’s official controls. v1.4.3 was tested in the mGBA engine on a computer; it was not tested on an iPhone or iPad.

guides.name: Windows & macOS
steps: Save inside the old game, then close mGBA. Copy the old .gba and its .sav into a dated backup folder. Keep that backup unchanged.
Check mGBA Settings → Paths for your Save games location. By default, saves are beside the game file; a custom path overrides this.
Extract the v1.4.3 ZIP into a new folder. Keep the file name Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba.
Copy your backed-up save into the save location with the matching name Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav. If a save is already there, back it up before replacing it.
Open the new game, confirm v1.4 on the title, then choose Continue. Do not load an old save state. Check party, Bag, Badges, money and location.
Save inside the game, close mGBA, reopen and confirm Continue loads your progress. Keep both the old backup and a fresh v1.4.3 backup.
guides.note: If your old game uses a personal file name, keep a matching .gba/.sav pair. If Continue is missing, recheck the file names and Settings → Paths before starting New Game. Saves from v1.0 to v1.4.2 were tested in the mGBA 0.10.5 engine; the graphical mGBA app itself was not automated.

guides.name: Android
steps: In the old game, SAVE from the START menu, then use Quick Menu → Close Content so RetroArch writes the save file.
Your save is the .srm file with the same name as the game, in RetroArch’s Save directory (Settings → Directory → Save Files). Copy it to a dated backup folder with a file manager.
Extract the v1.4.3 ZIP. Give the new .gba the same name as your old one, or rename a copy of your .srm to Pokemon - Project Blonde.srm: the save is matched by file name.
Load the new game with the mGBA core, confirm v1.4 on the title, then choose Continue. Do not use an old RetroArch save state. Check party, Bag, Badges, money and location.
Save inside the game, close the content and back up the new .srm. Keep the pre-update backup too.
guides.note: If Continue is missing, check the save file name and the Save Files directory before starting New Game. This procedure follows RetroArch’s documented controls; it was not tested on an Android device.

guide_data_from.why: v1.4.1 to v1.4.3 (r05 to r11) change no reachable game data the guide shows: they add code, blank content proven unused, re-order three wild level ranges whose levels stay the same (v1.4.2) and fix how followers are drawn (v1.4.3). Re-running tools/romx.py on r09 or later would lose the unreachable scripts its static walk counted, not real content.

releases.save_compatibility_short: Saves from v1.0, v1.1, v1.2 and v1.3 continue with an ordinary Continue. Back up first.
highlights: Overworld wild encounters: see wild Pokémon in the grass, caves and water of every region, and battle the one you walk into. Optional; CLASSIC stays the default.
Primal Reversion: Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon, with the Red and Blue Orbs from May and Brendan after the Silph Conspiracy.
One-time legendaries you have caught stay caught after League wins.
The Silph Conspiracy, partner battles and a new Elite Four member.
Johto, Kanto and Hoenn in one adventure, with Mega Evolution, the DexNav and Pokémon that follow you.
changelog: Overworld wild encounters (optional). START > OPTIONS > WILD ENCOUNTERS: OVERWORLD or CLASSIC. CLASSIC (the familiar random encounters) stays the default for new and existing saves. In OVERWORLD, wild Pokémon appear on the map in grass, caves and water across all regions, and walking into one starts that battle. The species, levels and odds are the same as CLASSIC, including time of day, mass outbreaks, DexNav, Repel and Keen Eye / Intimidate. Details: Pokémon swim on water (Magikarp flop and splash), are tinted underwater, hide in tall grass, stay put across seamless route borders and never appear on ledges you cannot reach. Ice Path, Shoal Cave and the Bug-Catching Contest have their own safe rules.
Primal Reversion: Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon in battle, with their abilities, weather and cries. After the Silph story, MAY gives the Red Orb and BRENDAN gives the Blue Orb in Littleroot Town.
One-time legendary and mythical Pokémon you have caught no longer reappear after another League win. Pokémon you defeated or fled from still return as before.
Teaching a TM no longer changes another Pokémon's level after using an EXP Candy that did not raise a level.
X Attack, X Speed and other battle stat items can be used on any active Pokémon in single battles, whatever its original party position.
JANINE’s words at the Reception Gate now follow the Silph Conspiracy story.
The GS BALL in the Ruins of Alph no longer returns after each League win once CELEBI has been caught.
Team Rocket Grunts in Silph Co. use Generation 1–3 Pokémon (11F now has Steelix).
MAY outside the lab in Littleroot leaves after the Vermilion dock scene, even if you never spoke to her.

Silph Co. 1F no longer has STEVEN's Hoenn starter giveaway (starters you already received are kept). After the siege, Silph Co. and its lift play the normal Silph music; the siege music continues through Giovanni's final scene.

SNORLAX no longer shows ARCHER's portrait. EXP Candy quantity icons are visible. POKéGEAR calls are spaced out (10 minutes between routine calls, none right after a battle; each rematch is announced once).
New ERIKA portrait. JANINE and VENOMOTH vanish in an ash puff. Mega Meganium and Mega Chimecho follower sprites corrected.
Wild encounter rate moderated.
Title screen shows v1.4.
known_limitations: PC storage stays at 14 boxes (420 Pokémon). The save memory of a GBA cartridge is full; more boxes would need a save-format change and are planned for a future update, not v1.4.

Overworld encounters (optional): on very busy screens a single frame can occasionally be dropped, as in CLASSIC. An area you can only reach by Surf still counts as reachable, so Pokémon may appear there before you have Surf. DexNav can sometimes report that the Pokémon could not be found nearby; try again.

Legendaries: for a legendary without its own "caught" record, one that was caught and then released or traded away can no longer be recognised and may reappear after a League win. Copies created by League wins in older versions are kept.
A GS BALL you already collected again in an older version stays in your bag.

v1.4 was tested in the mGBA 0.10.5 engine on a computer. It was not tested on original GBA hardware; the platform guides describe Android (RetroArch / mGBA core) and Delta (iOS) setup from their official documentation.

instructions: Back up the old game and its normal in-game save.
Use your platform guide: matching mGBA / RetroArch file names, or Delta import/export.
Cold launch and choose CONTINUE; do not transfer an old save state.
WILD ENCOUNTERS starts as CLASSIC; switch it in OPTIONS if you want overworld encounters.
Verify party, bag, badges, money and location, then save and back up again.
facts: Use Continue from a cold launch. Do not carry an emulator save state across this update. If you only have a save state, load it in the old version and make a normal in-game save first.
WILD ENCOUNTERS starts as CLASSIC. Switch it in START › OPTIONS if you want to see wild Pokémon on the map; you can switch back at any time.
If a Pokémon’s level was wrongly lowered by the old TM / EXP Candy bug, deposit it in the PC and withdraw it again, or let it gain experience, and its correct level returns.
A save made inside a building or town shows that place as it was in the old version. Leave and re-enter, and it updates. Nothing is lost.

The game file is still named Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba. Keep the matching save name: Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav in mGBA, Pokemon - Project Blonde.srm in RetroArch. If your files use another name, keep that matching pair on copies; do not rename or overwrite your only backup.
If Continue is missing, stop and check the imported save or the save path before starting a new game.
To go back, restore v1.3 with its own pre-update save backup.

guides.name: iPhone & iPad
steps: In the old game, use the game’s SAVE command. Return to Delta’s library.
Long-press the old game: Manage Save File → Export Save File. Save a dated backup in Files. Keep the old game and this backup.
Download the ZIP from the official Discord downloads post and extract it in Files. In Delta, tap + and import Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba. It may appear as a separate library entry.
Long-press the new game: Manage Save File → Import Save File. Select a copy of your exported save.
Cold-launch the new game, check the v1.4 label, then choose Continue. Check party, Bag, Badges, money and location.
Save inside the game and export a fresh backup. Keep the pre-update backup too.
guides.note: Use the normal save, not an emulator save state. If Continue is missing, check the save import before starting New Game. Delta accepts a save of exactly 131,072 bytes; a save exported from Delta already is, and a save from mGBA on a computer (131,088 bytes) must be trimmed first. This procedure was written from Delta’s official controls. v1.4 was tested in the mGBA engine on a computer; it was not tested on an iPhone or iPad.

guides.name: Windows & macOS
steps: Save inside the old game, then close mGBA. Copy the old .gba and its .sav into a dated backup folder. Keep that backup unchanged.
Check mGBA Settings → Paths for your Save games location. By default, saves are beside the game file; a custom path overrides this.
Extract the v1.4 ZIP into a new folder. Keep the file name Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba.
Copy your backed-up save into the save location with the matching name Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav. If a save is already there, back it up before replacing it.
Open the new game, confirm v1.4 on the title, then choose Continue. Do not load an old save state. Check party, Bag, Badges, money and location.
Save inside the game, close mGBA, reopen and confirm Continue loads your progress. Keep both the old backup and a fresh v1.4 backup.
guides.note: If your old game uses a personal file name, keep a matching .gba/.sav pair. If Continue is missing, recheck the file names and Settings → Paths before starting New Game. v1.0, v1.1 and v1.3 saves were tested in the mGBA 0.10.5 engine; the graphical mGBA app itself was not automated.

guides.name: Android
steps: In the old game, SAVE from the START menu, then use Quick Menu → Close Content so RetroArch writes the save file.
Your save is the .srm file with the same name as the game, in RetroArch’s Save directory (Settings → Directory → Save Files). Copy it to a dated backup folder with a file manager.
Extract the v1.4 ZIP. Give the new .gba the same name as your old one, or rename a copy of your .srm to Pokemon - Project Blonde.srm: the save is matched by file name.
Load the new game with the mGBA core, confirm v1.4 on the title, then choose Continue. Do not use an old RetroArch save state. Check party, Bag, Badges, money and location.
Save inside the game, close the content and back up the new .srm. Keep the pre-update backup too.
guides.note: If Continue is missing, check the save file name and the Save Files directory before starting New Game. This procedure follows RetroArch’s documented controls; it was not tested on an Android device.

changelog: A new postgame storyline. It begins once you are Champion of the Hoenn League: step outside and wait for a call from Brendan.
Follow the trail from Littleroot Town back to Kanto, through Vermilion Harbor to Saffron City.
Brendan and May join the investigation and fight alongside you in partner battles.
Kanto's Gym Leaders have their own parts to play, from the harbour to Saffron City.
Team Rocket has returned under Giovanni and Archer and taken Silph Co. Fight through the reopened tower: lifts, warp panels, security doors and more.
The back entrance of the Seafoam Gym is open again.
Story battles are built for a fully trained team, with opponents up to Lv.100 and Mega Evolution on both sides.
When the story is over, there is a change at the Indigo Plateau: Eusine joins the Elite Four with a team of his own.
Fully staged cutscenes with portraits, character movement and Pokémon companions, including Blue's Arcanine and Misty's Water Pokémon swimming in Vermilion Harbor.
New battle back sprites for Brendan and May in partner battles.

Partner battles: using a Revive while your partner had no Pokémon left could leave the game stuck on a party screen that could not be closed. Fixed for every battle fought alongside a partner, including the ones already in v1.2.
The title screen now displays v1.3 beneath PRESS START.
Everything added in v1.2 remains, including Hoenn's ambient Pokémon and the v1.2 hotfix (Ability Capsules and Ability Patches cannot be sold).
known_limitations: The Silph Conspiracy is postgame content for a strong team. It starts only after the Hoenn League has been won.
On the cooling-system floor of Silph Co., partial progress on the puzzle resets if you leave the floor or black out. Repeat the full sequence.

Very rarely, in a two-against-two battle fought alongside a partner, a move that knocks out several Pokémon at once can bring up a technical message screen. Press START and the battle continues. This was already the case in v1.2.
During scripted scenes your following Pokémon returns to its Poké Ball and comes back out when you regain control.

A save made inside a building or town shows that place as it was in the old version until you leave and re-enter it. Some character graphics also stay cached in older saves until the map is re-entered.
33 of Hoenn's ambient Pokémon stand close to a town entrance and can be seen appearing as you walk or Surf into the town. This is cosmetic (unchanged from v1.2).
Six of Hoenn's ambient land Pokémon first appear facing down rather than the direction they were designed to face (unchanged from v1.2).
Martin on Route 12 and Jake/Joyce on Route 26 keep inherited off-map placements (unchanged from v1.2).
Testing used the mGBA 0.10.5 emulator core on a computer. Delta on an iPhone/iPad, Android devices and physical hardware were not tested for this release.
Music and sound were not listened to or recorded during release testing.

Johto, Kanto and Hoenn in one adventure, on one save file.
482 Pokémon to find, including 42 regional forms.
Mega Evolution, the DexNav and Pokémon that follow you.
Cable-link trading and battles between two copies.
changelog: Hoenn's towns and cities are now alive with Pokémon: 125 ambient Pokémon across all 16, each chosen for its town.
They perch on rooftops, treetops and sea rocks, wander lawns, beaches and gardens, and gather in pairs and small groups.
41 of them can be spoken to and answer with their cry and a line.
Every Hoenn Gym has its Leader's Pokémon on the roof.
14 swim in open water in Petalburg, Lilycove, Mossdeep, Sootopolis, Pacifidlog and Ever Grande: Wailmer, Corsola, Luvdisc, Marill and Spheal.
The title screen now displays v1.2 beneath PRESS START.

Cold-launch the updated game, check the v1.1 label, then choose Continue. Check party, bag, Badges, money and location. Leave and re-enter the map if old NPC artwork is still visible.
Save inside the game and export a fresh backup. Keep the pre-update backup too.
guides.note: Use the normal save, not an old emulator save state. If Continue is missing, check the save import before starting New Game. This procedure was written from Delta’s official controls; v1.1 was not tested on an iPhone or iPad.

guides.name: Windows & macOS
steps: Save inside the old game, then close mGBA. Copy the old .gba and normal .sav into a dated backup folder. Keep that backup unchanged.
Check mGBA Settings → Paths for your Save games location. By default, saves are beside the game file; a custom path overrides this.
Download and extract the official Discord ZIP into a new folder. Keep the filename Pokemon - Project Blonde.gba.

Copy your backed-up normal save into the configured save location with the matching name Pokemon - Project Blonde.sav. If that path already has a save, back it up before replacing it. If you use a custom save path, make sure the backup is outside that active path.

Open the extracted .gba in mGBA, confirm v1.1 on the title, then select Continue. Do not load an old save state. Check party, bag, Badges, money and location; leave and re-enter the map to refresh cached NPC graphics.
Save inside the game, close mGBA, reopen and confirm Continue loads your progress. Keep both the old backup and a fresh v1.1 save backup.
guides.note: If your old game file uses a personal name, keep a matching .gba / .sav pair on copies. If Continue is missing, recheck filenames and Settings → Paths before starting New Game. Save migration was tested with the mGBA 0.10.5 engine; the mGBA application window itself was not automated.
